raw_response: For BNY Mellon, the 16% year-over-year decrease in reported expenses was primarily driven by the goodwill impairment associated with its investment management reporting unit that occurred in the third quarter of the previous year. For M&T Bank, the $15 million decrease in non-interest expenses compared to the linked quarter was due to $11 million in lower compensation and benefit costs (reflecting lower average headcount and contracted resources) and $6 million in lower other cost of operations (largely reflecting lower sub-advisory fees resulting from the sale of the CIT business).
